root_cause_label: Rave-family scanner plateaus at ~59% win rate vs stone.red despite extensive parameter tuning; 75% gate never crossed
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent converged on a Rave-style carpet-bombing scanner that plateaued at ~59% against stone.red across all variants and all parameter adjustments, never crossing the required 75% win-rate gate, and ultimately submitted the partial solution while correctly acknowledging the failure.
t_err_evidence: Step 44: First benchmark of reference Rave warrior vs stone.red yields Results: 59 40 1 (59% wins, well below the 75% threshold). Despite this clear ceiling, the agent subsequently decides at step 49 to 'create a modified Rave' rather than abandoning the scanner family for a fundamentally different approach.
t_commit_evidence: Step 73: After exhausting multiple Rave variants (steps 50-85) all plateauing near 59%, the agent's think step explicitly states 'I'll create a final warrior based on Rave but with [modifications]', formally committing to the Rave family as the final design. All subsequent actions are Rave-based with no exploration of alternative strategy families. Step 74 then creates my_warrior.red as a Rave-based warrior.
t_surface_evidence: Step 81: Comprehensive test of the final warrior (now Rave Optimized / Rave Warrior) against all five opponents shows Results: 59 40 1 vs stone - still below 75% - making the failure explicitly observable in one consolidated output.
trigger_explanation: After seeing Rave achieve 59% vs stone (step 44), the agent operated under the false premise that parameter tuning (changing IVAL, DJNOFF, CDIST, adding initial bombers) could push the scanner family past 75% against stone. In reality the ~59% is a structural ceiling for this warrior class against stone's dense DAT bombing pattern within the cycle budget. Every variant tested (steps 51, 57, 60, 76, 80, 83, 85) confirmed this ceiling, but the agent continued in the same direction.
forewarning_evidence: Step 44 shows Rave vs stone = 59/40/1 (below required 75%). Steps 51, 57, 60, 65 (1000 rounds: 594/395/11 = 59.4%), 72 (five runs each returning exactly '59 wins'), 76, 80, 83, 85 all show the same ~59% ceiling. The repeated identical outcome ('59 wins' every single run in step 72) is a clear forewarning signal ignored before t_commit at step 73.
